page_format: A3 landscape for readable engineering figures

sources.title: 01 / Separator geometry
sources.caption: Native mesh surfaces and a central fluid section. The ideal collector retains the lower geometry; the physical brine-outlet face is a wall. No standing pool is required.
sources.source: S100 preserved N4000 pair; native boundary and z=0 section geometry.

sources.title: 02 / What changes between the cases?
sources.caption: Shading shows geometric removal extents, not liquid. Percentages refer to height, not volume; Fluent selects cells by centroid elevation. The dotted line is the historical cutoff at y=+0.020 m.
sources.source: Verified geometry and S20-S100 elevation definitions; common lower datum y=-1.484584 m.

sources.title: 03 / All five cases: matched numerical history
sources.caption: Changing thickness changes inventory and removal. Larger removal is not evidence of successful collection when the source-inclusive mass balance remains open.
sources.source: G1 native reports, N1-4000; all five runs. Later histories are shown separately.

sources.title: 04 / Completed cases: late inventory and mass balance
sources.caption: All four completed cases retain drift and strong imbalance. The source is counted once; steady-iteration inventory slopes are not physical storage rates.
sources.source: S20/S40/S60/S80, N4001-5000; S100 has no complete prescribed late window.

sources.title: 05 / Full-height liquid fraction: first central plane
sources.caption: Liquid fraction: 0 = no liquid; 1 = all liquid. Dashed lines locate the collectors. S100 is a recovery snapshot at N4000, not an equivalent N5000 endpoint.
sources.source: Native phase-2 facet values at z=0; four final N5000 pairs and S100 recovery N4000.

sources.title: 06 / Full-height liquid fraction: orthogonal plane
sources.caption: The second plane exposes azimuthal differences. These are unconverged field snapshots; use them to understand liquid distribution, not to claim validated separation efficiency.
sources.source: Native phase-2 facet values at x=0; common 0-1 scale; S100 recovery N4000.

sources.title: 07 / Liquid fraction above the collector
sources.caption: Liquid-rich outer regions persist. Lower total inventory does not produce a uniform improvement at every height. All four planes lie above the maximum collector top.
sources.source: Original G1 comparison; y=0.5, 1.5, 3 and 5 m; native facets; S100 N4000, others N5000.

sources.title: 08 / Mixture speed above the collector
sources.caption: Common 0-80 m/s scale. These section snapshots do not show the full domain or the larger speed excursions recorded earlier in the runs.
sources.source: Original G1 comparison; native mixture velocity magnitude; same four planes and snapshot indices.

sources.title: 09 / Liquid speed above the collector
sources.caption: Common 0-80 m/s scale. Zero liquid speed in nearly liquid-free regions is not evidence of a stagnant liquid pool.
sources.source: Original G1 comparison; native phase-2 velocity magnitude; same four planes and snapshot indices.

sources.title: 10 / Residuals: every active equation
sources.caption: All four completed cases fail the 10^-3 throughout-final-window requirement for continuity, k, epsilon and liquid fraction. The three momentum equations pass that late-window indicator.
sources.source: Complete native residual histories N1-5000; seven equations; identical vertical limits across these four cases.

sources.title: 11 / S100: numerical failure
sources.caption: S100 was already unconverged at N4000. Epsilon, pressure and velocity escalated before the floating-point exception at attempted N4183. The failure cause and repeatability are not isolated.
sources.source: All seven native residuals; left N1-4100, right N4100-4182. Full N1-4182 records remain in the evidence bundle.

claim_limit: Unconverged discovery; S100 fields at recovery N4000, other cases final N5000
